messages:
Arjun Desai: quick q for folks: as we finalize batching defaults per SLO tier, how are we thinking about quantization variants interacting w/ batching knobs? e.g. fp16 vs fp8 vs int8/awq. i’m seeing perf “wins” flip depending on batch size + prefill/decode mix.

Jonas Weber: yeah, it’s not just perf. for some variants we hit correctness-ish issues under aggressive batching (esp longer prompts). we should be explicit: tier defaults assume a quant profile, or at least have compatibility constraints + fallback.

Hassan Mirza: +1. we’ve got 3 axes colliding:
1) quant kernel constraints (supported seq lengths / block sizes)
2) kv cache format (fp16 vs fp8 kv)
3) scheduler behavior (max_wait_ms, max_batch_tokens, prefill batching)

Claire Dubois: from evals side: when we pushed cost-efficient + awq on the “code” promptset, quality deltas were fine overall but we saw a higher rate of truncation / early stop when under overload (likely admission/backpressure causing shorter max decode / cancellation). so not purely “quant changes output”, but quant changes throughput => changes overload mode frequency.

Quentin Harris: model catalog metadata can help here. we already track “recommended_precision” per model family/hw class, but we need a second dimension: “batching_profile_compat”. some combos are technically supported but have bad tail (p99) b/c kernels pick different paths.

Lena Fischer: runtime side: scheduler doesn’t currently know quant profile explicitly. it knows “engine variant” + some kernel caps. we can add a signal like `effective_quant_profile` into the policy decision / reason codes, but please keep cardinality low.

Omar El-Sayed: for fast tier specifically: fp8 prefill on H100 is great until we hit mixed prompt-length batches; the prefill kernel ends up with less predictable latency spikes. with a tight wait budget we sometimes end up with underfilled batches anyway, so fp8 doesn’t buy as much as it does in standard/cost-efficient.

Noah Patel: we should separate:
- "supported" (won’t crash / numerically unstable)
- "recommended" (meets SLO gates w/ tier knobs)
- "discouraged" (works but fails perf gates / creates noisy tails)

Jonas Weber: agree. proposal: publish a small matrix by (model family, hw class, tier) -> default quant profile, with fallback rules.

Rina Kobayashi: for benchmark-lab, we can encode this as constraints so perf suite doesn’t accidentally pick unsupported combos. right now it just runs what’s in the candidate sheet.

Arjun Desai: can we sanity-check the most common combos we expect for launch?
- Llama-3 8B/70B on A100/H100
- Qwen2.5 7B/14B
- Mistral small-ish

Quentin Harris: current reality (rough):
- H100: fp8 weights OK for llama3 70b; kv cache fp8 experimental (some kernels only)
- A100: mostly fp16/bf16 weights; int8 works for some but depends on kernel set
- L4/A10: int8/awq more common; but long-context + large batches can be rough

Hassan Mirza: also: quant interacts with max_batch_tokens because some int8 paths have stricter shared memory usage; we hit “kernel falls back to slower path” when batch tokens exceed certain thresholds. tail latency explodes and then the scheduler tries to compensate (queue builds).

Lena Fischer: this matches what we saw in profiling. a lot of the “quant is slower” reports are actually “quant hit fallback kernel due to shape”. which is then determined by (prompt length buckets x batch size).

Noah Patel: so for the tiered batching defaults, we need a guardrail: if engine reports it’s on a fallback kernel path, cost-efficient tier should reduce aggressiveness (lower max_batch_tokens) or switch quant profile if available.

Omar El-Sayed: careful: switching quant profile dynamically is a bigger lever than we want for v1. but we can do a deterministic fallback at model-load time:
- if requested quant not compatible w/ tier profile, pick next-best quant that meets SLO
- else keep requested quant and adjust batching knob caps

Jonas Weber: +1. dynamic switching at runtime will make debugging impossible.

Sana Farid: for canary analysis, we should log *which* fallback happened (and why) so we can stratify metrics. otherwise we’ll see “cost-efficient tier worse” but it’s actually “cost-efficient tier mostly ran fp16 due to compat.”

Claire Dubois: reason codes should include quant compat so Console "why this profile" can say "cost-efficient requested but running standard quant due to model constraint".

Lena Fischer: what reason codes do folks want? something like:
- `PROFILE_SELECTED_TIER_DEFAULT`
- `PROFILE_SELECTED_OVERRIDE`
- `PROFILE_FALLBACK_QUANT_UNSUPPORTED`
- `PROFILE_FALLBACK_KERNEL_SHAPE_LIMIT`
- `PROFILE_FALLBACK_OVERLOAD_MODE`

Quentin Harris: `*_KERNEL_SHAPE_LIMIT` might be hard to keep stable across releases. could we phrase it as a capability flag from engine? e.g. `ENGINE_CAP_BATCH_TOKENS_MAX_EXCEEDED`.

Noah Patel: yes. engine can expose coarse caps: `max_prefill_batch_tokens`, `max_decode_batch_tokens` for the active quant+kernel set. scheduler clamps to those.

Hassan Mirza: important: those caps can be different per stage (prefill vs decode). cost-efficient wants to crank prefill batching, but decode has to be constrained for streaming. caps will force that split, which is fine as long as we expose it.

Rina Kobayashi: for perf suite, can we add a validation step: when a candidate profile is selected, assert `requested_max_batch_tokens <= engine_cap` and if not, record it as “clamped” + fail fast tier gates if clamping is frequent.

Jonas Weber: clamping shouldn’t necessarily fail; it just means your candidate profile isn’t actually what you think it is. but for publishing recommended profiles, we should avoid shipping ones that are always clamped.

Arjun Desai: ok, action items?
1) Quentin to draft minimal compat metadata fields for model catalog (quant profile + engine caps?)
2) Lena/Noah to confirm engine can expose stable caps + a single “compat class” per quant variant
3) Jonas/Claire to update quantization matrix doc to include “tier compatibility” section (supported vs recommended)
4) Rina to update benchmark harness to record clamping + reason code

Quentin Harris: yep, i’ll propose:
- `supported_quant_profiles`: list
- `recommended_quant_by_tier`: map (fast/standard/cost)
- `engine_cap_class`: e.g. `H100_FP8_V1`, `A100_FP16`, `L4_INT8_AWQ`
(not nested in the public doc, but internal metadata can be structured)

Lena Fischer: +1. for runtime metrics, we’ll log `engine_cap_class` as a low-card tag and avoid raw quant variant strings.

Claire Dubois: also adding to eval plan: when we benchmark tier defaults, we should hold quant fixed per run so we can attribute changes. otherwise perf+quality deltas get confounded.

Jonas Weber: cool. i’ll sync this into the quantization-profile-matrix doc + note “no runtime auto-switching in v1; only load-time selection + batching clamps.”

Arjun Desai: thanks all. this unblocks the “how do we explain cost-efficient tier” conversations too (i.e., it may be cost-efficient via batching *or* via quant, depending on compat).

Rina Kobayashi: i’ll add a perf suite annotation line in results like:
`effective_quant=H100_FP8_V1, requested_tier=cost_efficient, effective_tier=cost_efficient, clamped=true`
so we can grep quickly.

Noah Patel: perfect. and please make sure we don’t create a million combinations in metrics. keep it to tier + cap class + model family + region.

Lena Fischer: noted :thumbsup: i’ll take this to the scheduler reason codes PR so we don’t forget the compat path.

Jonas Weber: closing loop: if anyone has examples where quant + large batches changed output *directly* (not overload), drop them here. we have one hypothesis around fp8 accumulation + long context but not confirmed.

Claire Dubois: will do. i’ll link the experiment log entry once i clean it up.
